brief: A compact desk unit with a drawer, plus a spike at a corner where three bases meet to hold a small platform.

requirements.evidence: Five hex bases: full bases at (0,0),(1,0),(1,-1) and a north half base at (0,-1), plus the joint bolts from lockJoints. check_build reports meshClash clear and no loose-body warnings.
addDrawer on the cut face of the half base at (0,-1) (drawer:0#0,-1#cut, key s). The drawer is in the build and the mesh check is clear.

requirements.requirement: Spike at a corner where three bases meet
requirements.evidence: Mount-type spike spike:0#0,0|1,-1|1,0 at the junction shared by bases (0,0), (1,-1) and (1,0).
setSpikeAccessory platform-sm on that spike. A default spike refused the platform (TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED), so I replaced it with the mount variant.

capOpenFaces clashes with hex-drawer-frame-s (4.49 mm, limit 0.5), and the build was rolled back. I could not skip the drawer cell's faces by name, so 15 open faces remain uncapped. The OPEN_CAP_FACE info is the only remaining note.

finish.summary: Built a compact desk unit: three full bases plus a half base, a drawer on the half base's cut face, and a mount spike with a small platform at the three-base corner. Joints are locked and the mesh check is clear. Fifteen faces stay uncapped because the cap pass clashes with the drawer frame. I did not add props, since the brief did not ask for them. Material and load suitability are not checked by the configurator.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
